item.text: IBAC reviewed corruption risks in Victoria’s political donation and lobbying arrangements to propose regulatory reforms.
item.support: has identified several areas of risk in relation to donations and lobbying

item.text: It analysed Victoria’s rules, consulted stakeholders and considered experience from other jurisdictions and its own investigations.
item.support: conducted a detailed policy analysis of the issues under consideration

item.text: IBAC concluded that lobbying regulation inadequately protected the public interest and that stronger donation rules were needed at state and council levels.
item.support: the regulation of lobbying in Victoria is inadequate

item.text: It made four recommendations covering donation disclosure and enforcement, campaign expenditure, lobbying legislation and oversight of lobbyists.
item.support: IBAC recommends that the government introduce legislation to regulate lobbying at both the state and local levels of government

item.quote: A high-level review of lobbying regulation in other jurisdictions makes it clear that the regulation of lobbying in Victoria is inadequate.
The existing regulatory regime does not serve to fully protect the public interest and to restrain, or at least constrain, the disproportionate, excessive and privileged practices of lobbyists.
